title: The depth of a nonzero finite module over a Noetherian local ring is at most the dimension of its support
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], i.e. a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $M\neq0$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ be the set of prime ideals $\mathfrak p\subset R$ with $M_{\mathfrak p}\neq0$, where $M_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}M$, $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$, is the localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], and let $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ be the supremum of the integers $n\ge0$ for which there is a chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ of prime ideals of $R$ all lying in $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$. Then $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)\ge\operatorname{depth}(M)$, where $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)$ is the depth [def-weil-pbc-depth].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LK (lemma-bound-depth, lines 17813-17817), proof lines 17819-17835. Tag verified in tags/tags: 00LK,algebra-lemma-bound-depth

proof.text: Nakayama in its Mathlib contrapositive form Submodule.top_ne_ideal_smul_of_le_jacobson_annihilator, together with IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal_le_jacobson, gives maximalIdeal R • top ≠ top. Unfold IsLocalRing.depth and Ideal.depth and select the regular-sequence supremum branch.

For each M-regular list rs, use the already proved Mathlib candidate Module.supportDim_add_length_eq_supportDim_of_isRegular: dim Supp(M/(rs)M) + length(rs) = dim Supp(M). This theorem packages the induction and the successive dimension-drop equality of the original steps 2–4. Regularity gives Nontrivial (M/(rs)M) via IsRegular.quot_ofList_smul_nontrivial. Its support dimension is not bottom by Module.supportDim_ne_bot_of_nontrivial, hence is nonnegative in WithBot ℕ∞. Adding length(rs) gives length(rs) ≤ dim Supp(M).

The nonzero module M has support dimension different from bottom. Rewrite it as the coercion of its canonical WithBot.unbot value. WithBot.coe_le_coe reduces the bound for depth to an inequality in ℕ∞. Apply sSup_le to the bound on each regular-sequence length from the previous step. The proof also covers infinite support dimension and the empty regular sequence.
